sources.name: UNESCO IICBA, Kenya: Education Country Brief (January 2024)
KUCCPS student portal (programmes, cluster subjects and past cut-offs)

system.fact: Kenya's education system follows a 2-6-3-3-3 structure: two years of pre-primary, six of primary, six of secondary (three junior and three senior) and at least three of tertiary education.
The structure replaced the previous system to align with Kenya's competency-based curriculum.
The Kenya National Examinations Council (KNEC) is the government body that supervises national examinations.
In 2021 KNEC developed a competency-based assessment framework, moving from a single final evaluation to ongoing formative and summative assessment.
Gross enrolment in tertiary education was 13% for men and 10% for women in 2017 (World Bank and UNESCO Institute for Statistics, as cited in the brief).

placement.fact: Students are placed into degree programmes at public universities and colleges by the Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service (KUCCPS).
The KUCCPS student portal lists, for each degree programme, the cluster subjects that count and the cut-off points of recent KCSE years at each institution.

pending.why: The KUCCPS portal blocked automated access from our servers on 10 November 2026, and the cluster-point formula is not yet confirmed from an official document. We do not publish rules or cut-offs we have not read from the official source.
route: Request a data file of programmes, cluster subjects and cut-offs from KUCCPS
Or have a person in Kenya collect them from the portal, with a second person checking
Confirm the cluster-point formula from a KUCCPS or Ministry of Education document
